newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-NO ACTION TAKEN ON REALIGNMENT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-NO ACTION TAKEN ON REALIGNMENT.

text.p: Major League Baseball's Executive Council met all day Thursday to discuss four or five proposals for realignment but reported no consensus and decided to hold a conference call with other owners on Friday.
The owners could be ready to approve a major overhaul of baseball's league and divisional alignments to take effect just one season after interleague play began this year.
Acting commissioner Bud Selig and Twins owner Carl Pohlad are among those pushing hardest for realignment in time for the 1998 season.
One scenario receiving consideration involves reducing each league from the current three to two divisions, with one league having 16 teams and the other 14.

Baseball expands to 30 teams next season with the addition of the expansion Arizona Diamondbacks and Tampa Bay Devil Rays. Arizona was tentatively placed in the National League and Tampa Bay in the American.
The 16-14 plan, said to be favoured by Selig, includes radical realignment with several teams swapping leagues in order to set up geographic rivalries.
The Western Division in one league would consist of the Anaheim Angels, Los Angeles Dodgers, Oakland Athletics, San Francisco Giants, Colorado Rockies, Seattle Mariners, San Diego Padres and Arizona.
The Central Division would include the Texas Rangers, Houston Astros, Chicago Cubs, Chicago White Sox, Kansas City Royals, St. Louis Cardinals, Milwaukee Brewers and Minnesota Twins.
The other league would have an East Division with the Baltimore Orioles, Boston Red Sox, Montreal Expos, New York Mets, New York Yankees, Philadelphia Phillies and Toronto Blue Jays.
The Atlanta Braves, Cincinnati Reds, Cleveland Indians, Detroit Tigers, Florida Marlins, Pittsburgh Pirates and Tampa Bay would make up the other division.
Four teams in each league would continue to make the playoffs in the 16-14 plan.
